orbits.scope: Relative Ab-to-Aa interferometric orbit. All published intervals are 2.3-97.7 percentiles, approximately two sigma; an alternative node/argument plus 180 degrees is allowed. Physical axis uses the publication distance, not the legacy component parallax.

axisSource.scope: Published adopted distance and error are at two sigma.

totalDynamicalMass.scope: Total Aa+Ab mass, with two-sigma bounds; never an individual component mass.

orbits.scope: Confirmed close spectroscopic binary with explicitly normalized Aa/Ab labels. The source publishes an argument of periastron of 255.6 +/- 12.2 degrees, but no astrometric node. Leave the rendered sky orientation unavailable; do not invent a node or ambiguous argument convention.

Circular eclipsing-binary orbit; period and inclination adopted from Torres & Ribas 2002. The fitted HJD0=2449345.116643 +/- 0.000068 is an eclipse reference, not a periastron epoch. Node, argument and periastron remain unavailable rather than fabricating sky geometry.

Global relative binary solution. Listed orbital uncertainties are formal MCMC errors from Table 6, distinct from the profile-likelihood physical-parameter errors adopted for the stellar masses/radii. Preserve the publication distance assumption; no individual constant orbital velocities are assigned.
orbits.uncertaintyConvention: Formal Table 6 MCMC uncertainties; source separates these from profile-likelihood errors.

axisSource.scope: Formal joint-solution MCMC distance; abstract/profile-likelihood distance is 24.30 +/- 0.05 pc.

epochSource.sourceConvention: Equation 5; combined fit dates are HJD minus 2400000, not MJD.

orbits.orientationValidation: Relative secondary offsets reproduce the signed Table 3 positions at MJD 60232.4493, 60234.5388 and 60259.3951 when observation times are converted to HJD. No 180-degree primary-argument conversion is applied to the published combined sky solution.
